neighbours.label: noun naming a technology or device, as the subject of a sentence about it (phones, televisions, DRAMs)
fire: In the early days, personal computers were sold mostly to hobbyists.
Within a decade, laptops had replaced desktop machines in many offices.
By 1980, videocassette recorders were common in middle-class homes.
Over the years, smartphones became the main way people read the news.
At first, radios were large wooden cabinets that stood in the living room.
Eventually, digital cameras made film processing nearly obsolete.
For a while, pagers were the standard tool for doctors on call.
After the war, refrigerators became affordable for ordinary families.
quiet: In the early days, wild horses were found mostly on the open plains.
Within a decade, oak trees had replaced the grass in many fields.
By 1980, coyotes were common in many suburban neighborhoods.
Over the years, the liver becomes better at processing certain foods.
At first, tadpoles are small dark creatures that stay near the bottom.
Eventually, the bones of the skull fuse into a single solid structure.
For a while, the river was the main source of water for the valley.
After the storm, the wildflowers bloomed across the whole hillside.

notes: Card top: attribute, telephones, issues, DRAMs, HDTVs, surgery; output promotes past-tense verbs (did, was, became). Probe: tech nouns 0.30-0.46 in past and present, 'thyroid gland' 0.04. Near misses put body or nature nouns in the same slot.
